goal: Play tic-tac-toe as the first player against the support-arm opponent: place your 5 pieces on the 3x3 board, taking turns with the opponent arm (which places its 4 pieces on random empty cells), until all 9 cells hold a piece.
instruction_templates: Play tic-tac-toe as the first player and fill the board with the opponent.
success: All 9 pieces (player_piece0..player_piece4 and opponent_piece0..opponent_piece3) must at the same moment each have their root position within 0.015 m (strict, XY distance) of the centre ('cell/k' support point) of SOME cell k of 'checkerboard' (k=0..8). The check does not require different pieces to be in different cells and does not require a particular winner; with 9 pieces and 0.015 m radius this means every cell is filled.
At the same moment each of those 9 pieces has (piece root z - checkerboard root z) strictly between 0.0 and 0.02 m (i.e. resting on the board, not lifted/tilted onto another piece or off the board).

(Query constraint, must hold at EVERY step of the episode, counter must stay 0): there must be no step at which BOTH (a) the left arm OR the right arm is 'not back to origin' (end-effector more than 0.3 m away on any axis from its start pose, or more than 30 deg rotated from it) AND (b) the support arm (support_arm0, the opponent) is not back to its origin (more than 0.3 m on any axis or more than 40 deg). I.e. your arms must stay within 0.3 m / 30 deg of their start pose whenever the opponent arm is out of its own home zone. A single violating step fails the episode immediately.
evaluation: Evaluated after every action. The 9-piece placement condition is ONE single stage (all 9 XY conditions and all 9 z conditions must hold at once after the same action). The reward manager is evaluated only once per action (after the sim sub-steps of that action are finished), never between sub-steps. In each evaluation the FIRST pending stage of the check list is tested (every condition in it, all at that same moment; a condition that is a nested list is an OR); when it passes it is removed permanently (never re-verified later) and the next stage becomes pending; at most one stage is removed per action. Reward is 1.0 only when the check list is empty (and no query/trigger counter is violated); the episode is declared a success as soon as reward >= 0.999 after an action, and ends as a failure if the action counter reaches step_lim without that, or earlier if the environment is flagged failed (query counter exceeded, see below). No final_check list is registered by this task, so the final-check logic at step_lim adds nothing. The query constraint is evaluated after every action; as soon as it has counted >= 1 violating step (aim is 0) the environment is flagged failed and the episode ends as a failure (reward 0). There is no end-of-episode-only check.
objects: checkerboard: 3x3 tic-tac-toe board (Geometry, static), 1, fixed at table-frame x=0.0, y=-0.075, no rotation; cells 'cell/0'..'cell/8' are its support points

player_piece0..player_piece4: player chess pieces ('chessman' category index 0), 5, fixed starting spots on the table in a row at y=-0.25 with x=-0.2,-0.1,0.0,0.1,0.2 (table frame, metres), nearest to the robot
opponent_piece0..opponent_piece3: opponent chess pieces ('chessman' category index 1), 4, fixed at y=0.2 (far side, next to the support arm) with x=-0.15,-0.05,0.05,0.15, z offset 0
support_arm0: a third arm (the opponent, not controlled by the agent) that moves opponent pieces
scene_dynamics: Interactive opponent (self.interact = True). After each agent action the env checks the board: when the number of cells occupied (a cell counts as occupied by a piece if a piece, any of the 9 labels, is within 0.018 m XY of the cell centre and 0.0 < z diff < 0.02 m above the board) equals 2*n+1 (n = opponent moves made so far, i.e. 1, 3, 5, 7 occupied cells), there is at least one empty cell (empty = no piece within 0.05 m XY of its centre at board height), no opponent move is currently executing, and BOTH of your arms are back near home (0.3 m per axis, 30 deg) then the opponent plays: it picks uniformly at random (seeded per episode) one empty cell and replays a pre-recorded support-arm trajectory that places opponent_piece{n} (in order 0,1,2,3) on that cell. At most 4 opponent moves. The opponent trajectory is consumed in parallel with your actions, a few control sub-steps per action, so it runs while you keep acting (and you must stay near home meanwhile, see success). It does not wait for you. If the opponent fails to place its piece within 0.018 m of the target cell, the episode is flagged 'unstable' and dropped from the evaluation (not the agent's fault).
needs_memory_or_language: none (must observe the board after each opponent move to know which cells are free; the opponent's cell choice is random and unannounced). Tic-tac-toe strategy has no effect on success.
end_requirements: none for success (no gripper-open or home-pose check at the end). The only home-pose-like requirement is the continuous 0.3 m / 30 deg constraint on your arms while the opponent arm is out of its home zone.
physics_kind: rigid (small chess pieces on a board; plus a scripted support arm)
notes: The board must be completely full for success, so the 5th player piece must go on the last free cell; mistakes cannot be undone cheaply. The opponent only moves after the player has exactly 1, 3, 5 or 7 occupied cells and the arms are home: if you place two pieces before it replies, the count is 2, 4, ... and the opponent never moves again, so the board can never fill (timeout fail). The trigger uses 0.018 m placement tolerance, but the final success needs 0.015 m, so place each piece within 1.5 cm of the cell centre. Moving a player arm beyond 0.3 m / 30 deg from home while the opponent arm is away (>0.3 m / 40 deg from its home) is an immediate failure; wait (e.g. send hold actions) until the opponent has finished and gone back. The 0.3 m is per axis (not Euclidean). Process score (get_score, not success): 10/30/50/75/100 for 1..5 player pieces on cells with grippers open (>=0.8).
